subject: Re: Severe throttling during nightly ingestion — burst credit leakage?

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@acmecorp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-18T23:14:00Z
Subject: Nightly ingestion spike — 429s and huge latency

Hi Laura,

We saw a big failure window during our nightly ingest at ~22:45 PT where 40% of requests returned 429 and the rest suffered 2-4s additional tail latency. This is on our "bulk_embedding" route that normally runs at ~300 qps. The job retried and backed off but it prolonged the processing and caused several downstream pipelines to miss SLA.

Attached is a small traffic dump and screenshots from our dashboard. The error body shows "quota_exceeded: burst credits depleted" in some responses but the quota page still shows ~20% headroom on the reserved capacity. Can you help investigate? This is blocking our production batch for tomorrow.

Samantha
Samantha Lee

Samantha@acmecorp.com

Thanks Laura — looking. Samantha, quick note from infra side: the symptom you describe (429s with an apparent headroom on reserved capacity) matches a class of incidents we've seen when burst-credit accounting gets out of sync with the per-tenant quota window during rapid reserve/renew cycles.

What I need immediately:
- the raw traffic dump you attached (we have it) plus the exact timestamps and the outbound client IP(s) if possible
- whether you were running with pinned model version or allowing model fallback (affects kernel selection and per-request token cost)

I'll start by pulling credit-reconciliation logs and the per-tenant safety-valve actions around 22:30-23:00 PT. If we confirm a leak, remediation will be: temporary quota bump (10-20%) for Acme, revert the aggressive safety valve, and ship a reconciliation fix to the rate-limiter within 24h.

I'll update in 30–45 minutes with findings.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, samantha@acmecorp.com
Date: 2028-10-19T09:10:00Z
Subject: Action plan and temporary mitigation — Acme ingestion impact

Update from ops after initial triage: we've reproduced a reconciliation gap in the burst-credit ledger for Acme when concurrency jumps >2.3x inside a single quota window. The ledger incorrectly deducted credits for short-lived preflight requests (health probes + client retries) and then failed to refund them on the next window boundary because of a race in the safety-valve state machine. That left the tenant appearing to have exhausted burst credits while there was reserved capacity available — hence 429s and high tail latency as requests contended for throttled slots.

Immediate mitigation deployed at 09:02 PT:
- temporary burst_credit allowance: +25% for tenant (applied)
- disabled the aggressive safety-valve auto-debit for 30 minutes (rolled back to conservative mode)
- increased logging of per-request credit lifecycle to detect further leaks

Requested follow-ups:
1) Karthik to open a patch (rate-limiter reconciliation) and target a 12h hotfix window.
2) Rishi to coordinate SMS/exec alerting for high-severity customer throttles and confirm whether we should offer a one-time bill credit for Acme's SLA miss.
3) Laura to confirm with Acme that the temporary allowance is sufficient for their backfill and whether they'd like Redwood to run a replay on a staging cluster.

We'll monitor for 2 hours and post a post-mortem after the hotfix.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-10-19T16:42:00Z
Subject: Root cause and next steps — burst credit reconciliation race

Findings summary (root cause):
- The rate-limiter has a race between the window-rollover goroutine and the safety-valve debit path. Under a rapid concurrency spike we saw: (A) preflight/health checks and client retries cause transient extra debit writes; (B) the rollover path batches refunds at end-of-window but skips entries marked by an in-flight safety-valve op; (C) those entries are never reconciled until manual intervention. Net effect: tenant appears to have 0 burst credits despite reserved capacity being available.

Impact: Acme experienced ~9 minutes of 429s and elevated p95 latency; we saw retry storms that amplified the window.

Planned technical remediation (timeline):
- Hotfix (12h target): guarantee idempotent refund writes and add a reconciliation sweep at window-rollover. (Patch branch: fix/rate-reconcile-9421)
- Medium (48h): add a hedged-update pattern to safety-valve to prevent stalls under concurrent ops.
- Long (2 weeks): change accounting to per-request tokens (instead of aggregated credits) to reduce edge-case accounting errors.

Customer remediation and comms:
- temporary +25% burst allowance applied at 09:02 PT — confirmed by Acme as adequate to finish backfill.
- Ops will propose a goodwill credit for the SLA miss; Rishi to confirm amount.
- Post-mortem to be shared with Acme by 2028-10-21 COB.

Action items assigned:
- karthik_iyer: open PR, run staging replay against Acme dump, verify fixes (12h)
- marissa_cole: schedule 2h watch window and compile logs for post-mortem (6h)
- rishi_malhotra: draft customer credit proposal and exec note (24h)
- laura_bennett: run replay offer with customer and confirm customer-supplied windows (ASAP)

I'll keep the thread updated with CI results.
